newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Dec 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Dec 11.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- HOMES MINNOW MARCHES IN TO SWEEP UP SAINTS

Secure Retirement, a tiny retirement housing company, yesterday made a surprise 10 million pound stg takeover of Premier League Southampton. The move will enable it to exit the retirement property market as the climate becomes ever more favorable for football flotations.
-- CARLTON TAKES 17 MILLON POUND STAKE IN GETTY GROUP

Carlton Communications is spending 17 million pounds stg on a 10 percent stake in media business Getty Communications. The two companies will collaborate in post-production and editing of images and Getty will use the proceeds for further acquisitions of image collections, archive photography and news footage.
-- BRITISH LAND'S FOCUS TURNS CLOSER TO HOME

Property group British Land yesterday announced 100 million pounds stg of asset sales since March, including all its overseas buildings. The company said it would concentrate its future activities in Britain and Ireland, particularly in Dublin. Interim profits in the half-year to September rose from 24.9 million pounds stg to 34.3 million pounds, and earnings per share more than doubled to 5.4p.
THE TIMES
-- CLARKS TO SPIN OFF FACTORY OUTLETS IN SHAKE-UP

The UK's second largest private company, C&J Clark, is planning to sell off its fast growing factory outlet operations as it attempts to refocus its core shoe manufacturing and retailing business. An outright disposal could raise 50 million pounds stg, but Clarks is believed to prefer a joint venture, with the long term plan of floating the business.
-- NORTHERN FIGHTS BID WITH MERGER

Northern Electric attempted yesterday to fend off CE Electric's unwanted bid advances, announcing plans to merge a large part of its business with another electricity company. Northern have not revealed which company it is having talks with to merge its electricity and gas supply operations, but Hydro-Electric and United Utilities are thought to be the most likely candidates.
-- A&L CAUTIOUS AS MEMBERS BACK CHANGE

The Alliance & Leicester Building Society got the thumbs up from members for conversion to a bank yesterday when 96 percent of saving members and 97 percent of borrowers voted in favour of the conversion. Despite this, the board may still attempt to delay the flotation because it fears proposals in the Building Societies bill that could lead to a takeover bid after flotation.
THE GUARDIAN
-- BCCI FRAUD VICTIMS PAID 1 BILLION POUNDS

Victims of the BCCI collapse yesterday received their first payments since the bank failed in 1991. Nearly 1 billion pounds stg was paid out to 30,000 creditors around the world in a share-out equivalent to 24.5p in the pound. A second payment is expected within 16 months, and a third is dependent on the success of legal action.
-- COSTAIN SELLS COAL AND LAND STAKES

Troubled construction group Costain yesterday announced it had found buyers for its US coal business and its share in the Spitalfields development in London. Despite the sales, the group is still in trouble and as net assets now total less than half of share capital, an extraordinary general meeting will be held on January 6 next year.
-- HINCHCLIFFE LOSES ARGUMENT OVER FACIA LIQUIDATOR

Stephen Hinchcliffe yesterday failed to persuade creditors of his collapsed Facia retail group to appoint the liquidator of his choice. Instead, creditors chose accountancy firm BDO Stoy Hayward. It emerged at the creditors' meeting that there is only enough money available to pay about 3.75p in the pound.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- BROKER DEALS 200 MILLION POUNDS BLOW TO RJB SHARES

Britain's biggest coal producer, RJB Mining saw 200 million pounds stg knocked off its market capitalization after its own stockbroker, BZW, downgraded its profits forecasts. BZW's research report focused attention on RJB's ability to compete with cheaper imports of coal from overseas in the wake of sterling's rapid recent appreciation.
-- BARCLAYS DEAL WITH MORGAN 'RISKS 600 JOBS'

As a result of Barclays' decision to sell part of its global custody service to Morgan Stanley, more than 600 jobs are at risk. Bifu, the banking union, said the job losses would be a devastating blow to Trowbridge, the Wiltshire town where much of Barclays' custody business is placed. The fears were expressed as Guardian Royal Exchange, the insurance group, said it would be cutting 350 jobs as part of a restructuring of its area and branch network.
-- LARGE OPPOSES WATCHDOG REFORM

Chairman of the Securities and Investments Board, Sir Andrew Large, has dismissed proposals by other City regulators who have been backing a radical reform of the financial policing system, calling the ideas they favour disruptive and time consuming. The ideas that are supported by the Securities and Futures Authority and the Personal Investment Authority include a shake-up in which regulation is split along functional lines between a body responsible for the health of financial institutions and a second organization devoted to financial consumer protection.
